facts.text: - Evidence: LTM derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose from 3,276 (FY2025) to 3,918 (LTM Q3 2026) while principal debt moved from 20,232 to 20,168 and cash from 1,309 to 2,485. - Mechanism: the improvement is earnings and cash driven. Gross debt is flat, so gross leverage of 5.15x at Q3 2026 depends on earnings continuing at the higher level; the company's own guidance for full year adjusted EBITDA of 4,315 to 4,415 (Q3 release page:4) is a management forecast, not a reported figure. - Perimeter: Bausch + Lomb contributes 328 of the Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of 1,350 and 5,065 of the 20,168 debt (Q3 release page:28; page:127). Its cash and revolver availability are generally not available to the parent group (page:127, page:131). Parent-group net debt is 13,130 against consolidated net debt of 17,683. - Interest burden: net interest expense of 1,162 for nine months 2026 is a P&L figure reduced by premium amortization; contractual interest is higher. Interest paid in FY2025 was 1,810 against net interest expense of 1,556. The company expects about 561 of interest payments in Q4 2026 (page:133) and the Remaining Secured Notes alone carry 4,017 of scheduled interest payments from the remainder of 2026 to 2032 (page:130). - Credit implication: leverage is falling but remains high for a group rated Caa2 and B- at the corporate level. Cover on cash interest in FY2025 was 1.81x. The risk is concentrated in 2028 to 2031 maturities and in the structural separation between the parent group and Bausch + Lomb.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The transaction history that matters to creditors is structural. Since 2022 the company has moved Bausch + Lomb shares into a holding company, 126NumberCo, and in 2025 used those shares as collateral for new first-lien debt that extended maturities from 2025 through 2028 to 2030 through 2032 (page:82, page:83). The Existing Senior Secured Notes are structurally subordinated to liabilities of 126NumberCo and to debt secured by assets outside their collateral such as the Bausch + Lomb share collateral (page:39), and the Senior Unsecured Notes are not guaranteed by 126NumberCo or 153NumberCo (page:130). Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are excluded from the parent's financial maintenance covenant (page:40). Creditors therefore hold a claim on a group whose most valuable subsidiary sits in a separate credit silo, and the company has described a full separation of Bausch + Lomb as subject to targeted leverage ratios and approvals (page:10). Net proceeds from any sale of the pledged shares must be applied to prepay the 2025 term loan and the 2032 notes pro rata (page:33, page:38).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability and concentration. Evidence: Salix is about 27% of revenue and about 47% of segment profit, Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix, growth was price-led (price 504, volumes down 173), a negotiated price starts January 1, 2027 and generic entry is expected in 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:75, page:123, page:96, page:98). Risk mechanic: the product that earns the largest share of segment profit faces a price reset and then volume erosion just as 2028 maturities of 3,766 become due (CP-1). Credit implication: refinancing capacity in 2028 depends on how much Xifaxan cash flow remains, which makes monitoring of Xifaxan sales, the 2027 price effect and the generic timeline a leading indicator for refinancing risk. Counter-evidence: Salix profit rose 28% in nine months 2026 and management raised guidance; neither tests the post-2027 level. 2. Structural subordination and the Bausch + Lomb silo. Evidence: first-lien claims at 126NumberCo hold the pledged Bausch + Lomb shares, and other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind (page:31, page:39); Bausch + Lomb's net debt and earnings are outside the covenant perimeter (page:40). Risk mechanic: value from the Bausch + Lomb stake flows first to the 2025 term loan and 2032 notes through the sweep (page:33, page:38). Credit implication: recovery prospects for notes outside that structure depend on residual value in the shares and on Bausch Health (excl. B+L) assets, with no expected recovery stated here. 3. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose to 3,918 on an LTM basis, while FY2025 cash interest cover was 1.81x on interest paid of 1,810 (CP-1). Risk mechanic: high cash interest and premium accounting mean P&L interest understates cash cost. Credit implication: cover is modest on a cash basis, so a decline in Salix profit would reduce cover quickly. 4. Sponsor and governance alignment. Evidence: no dividends and a small buyback, an issuer-level pattern of maturity extension, but unresolved participation terms in exchanges and overlapping leadership of two listed entities (page:127, page:76, page:138). Credit implication: mixed; the pack neither shows leakage nor tests the indentures' restrictions. 5. Key uncertainties. The covenant ratio and its step-up date, the debt document baskets, and the 2028 maturity wall (CP-0, CP-1).

rows.label: A Xifaxan-dependent U.S. pharmaceutical business sits in one group with Bausch + Lomb through a collateralised holding structure; Salix growth is price-led and Xifaxan faces a Medicare price in 2027 and expected generics in 2028.
Salix is about 27% of nine-month 2026 revenue but about 47% of segment profit, and Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix.
Salix revenue growth of 343 came from price of 504, partly offset by lower volumes of 173 after exiting certain channels.
211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares are pledged to the 2025 facilities and 2032 notes at 126NumberCo, which ranks ahead of other creditors' claims on those shares.
Documented actions since 2022 include an unrestricted subsidiary designation, a distressed exchange and a 2025 exchange that extended maturities; participation terms are not in the pack.
The Bausch Health chief executive is also interim chief executive and chairman of Bausch + Lomb, and a 50 buyback was authorised.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Bausch Health is a highly leveraged, structurally complex credit that is improving but not yet resilient. Its strongest support is liquidity and momentum: USD 2,485 million of consolidated cash and USD 1,135 million of undrawn revolvers at September 30, 2026, derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million, and debt to that EBITDA down from 6.18x to 5.15x [CP-1]. Its weakest point is dependence on Salix and Xifaxan, about 47% of segment profit, which faces a negotiated Medicare price from 2027 and expected generics in 2028, just before USD 3,766 million of debt falls due in 2028 [CP-1A, CP-1]. The outcome turns on how much Xifaxan cash flow survives 2027, and on whether USD 13,452 million due in 2028 to 2031 is refinanced inside a structure that ranks Bausch + Lomb value to the 2025 first-lien debt first.

citations.quote: Bausch Health is a highly leveraged, structurally complex credit that is improving but not yet resilient. Its strongest support is liquidity and momentum: USD 2,485 million of consolidated cash and USD 1,135 million of undrawn revolvers at September 30, 2026, derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million, and debt to that EBITDA down from 6.18x to 5.15x [CP-1]. Its weakest point is dependence on Salix and Xifaxan, about 47% of segment profit, which faces a negotiated Medicare price from 2027 and expected generics in 2028, just before USD 3,766 million of debt falls due in 2028 [CP-1A, CP-1]. The outcome turns on how much Xifaxan cash flow survives 2027, and on whether USD 13,452 million due in 2028 to 2031 is refinanced inside a structure that ranks Bausch + Lomb value to the 2025 first-lien debt first.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Leverage is falling but high. Consolidated principal debt of USD 20,168 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 20,232 million at December 31, 2025) over derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million gives 5.15x gross and 4.51x net, against 6.18x and 5.78x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Debt barely moved, so the improvement comes from earnings and from cash rising to USD 2,485 million. [Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is a derived Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure.] 2. The parent group deleveraged in Q3 2026. Bausch Health (excl. B+L) net debt fell from USD 13,651 million to USD 13,130 million, a reduction of USD 521 million in the quarter, while its debt was USD 15,103 million [CP-1]. Bausch + Lomb debt was USD 5,065 million and its cash and revolver are generally not available to the parent [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the net debt figures are derived.] 3. Liquidity is adequate near term but thinner at the parent. Consolidated cash plus undrawn revolvers was USD 3,620 million; the parent's share was USD 2,442 million (cash USD 1,973 million including restricted cash, plus USD 469 million undrawn) [CP-1]. The USD 643 million 2027 notes will be redeemed from cash on November 30, 2026, which reduces parent liquidity to about USD 1,799 million pro forma [CP-1, calculation below]. [Analyst Interpretation.] 4. The maturity wall starts in 2028. Debt maturing is USD 15 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 701 million in 2027, USD 3,766 million in 2028, USD 1,667 million in 2029, USD 4,123 million in 2030 and USD 3,896 million in 2031, with USD 6,000 million thereafter [CP-1]. The parent's 2028 maturities of USD 2,326 million exceed its pro forma liquidity of about USD 1,799 million, so repayment relies on cash generation or refinancing; the revolver also has an earlier-maturity trigger tied to indebtedness above USD 1,000 million [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.] 5. Earnings quality is price-led and concentrated. Salix revenue rose USD 343 million in nine months 2026 on price of USD 504 million, partly offset by volumes down USD 173 million, and Salix is about 27% of revenue but about 47% of segment profit [CP-1A]. Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix, faces a negotiated Medicare price from January 1, 2027 and expected generics in 2028, and the company impaired Salix goodwill by USD 1,426 million in January 2026 after failed Phase 3 trials [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the concentration shares are derived.] 6. Cash interest absorbs a large share of earnings. FY2025 cash interest was USD 1,810 million against derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,276 million, about 55% of it and a cover of 1.81x, and the pack gives no interim cash interest [CP-1]. Premium accounting makes P&L interest lower than cash interest, so cover on a P&L basis (2.53x LTM Q3 2026) is flattered [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact for inputs; Analyst Interpretation on direction.] 7. Structure matters as much as leverage. The 2025 first-lien debt at 126NumberCo holds a lien on 211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares, and sales proceeds must prepay it pro rata with the 2032 notes; other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind, and Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are outside the covenant [CP-1A]. Legal capacity and exchange terms cannot be tested without the debt documents. [Documentary Fact.] 8. Governance evidence is mixed rather than adverse. No dividends and a USD 50 million buyback authorised, a cash repurchase of near-par unsecured notes in 2025 and extended maturities weigh against overlapping leadership of two listed entities and unresolved terms of exchanges [CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

FY2025 cash interest was USD 1,810 million against derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,276 million, about 55% of it and a cover of 1.81x, and the pack gives no interim cash interest [CP-1]. Premium accounting makes P&L interest lower than cash interest, so cover on a P&L basis (2.53x LTM Q3 2026) is flattered [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact for inputs; Analyst Interpretation on direction.]

7. Structure matters as much as leverage. The 2025 first-lien debt at 126NumberCo holds a lien on 211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares, and sales proceeds must prepay it pro rata with the 2032 notes; other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind, and Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are outside the covenant [CP-1A]. Legal capacity and exchange terms cannot be tested without the debt documents. [Documentary Fact.]

8. Governance evidence is mixed rather than adverse. No dividends and a USD 50 million buyback authorised, a cash repurchase of near-par unsecured notes in 2025 and extended maturities weigh against overlapping leadership of two listed entities and unresolved terms of exchanges [CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases cover the annual and three quarterly reporting periods and the debt, liquidity and covenant text that the downstream work needs, so analysis can proceed with stated limitations. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture or lease document is supplied, so covenant definitions and the reported covenant ratio cannot be checked. |

| The only financial maintenance covenant text is on the revolving facility, and its step-up date is defined in a document not supplied. | Covenant headroom cannot be computed from the pack. | High |
| Debt maturities and revolver availability are printed in the latest quarterly report. | Liquidity and the maturity wall can be built from printed figures. | High |

### Readiness view

The effective source set can support all four requested consumers with bounded limitations. The three quarterly reports and the annual report are filed documents with consolidated statements, a financing note, a covenant description and liquidity discussion. The three releases add management-defined adjusted measures, segment revenue and guidance, and are attributed supporting claims, not controlling facts. The command sheet reads CP-1 RUN, CP-1A RUN, CP-2 RUN and CP-5 RUN, each READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, because the missing items (executed debt agreements, a covenant compliance figure, Bausch + Lomb's own filings) narrow depth and do not remove the statements those consumers need.
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025 statements (10-K, auditor report at page:212; balance sheet at page:218; cash flows at page:220) and unaudited Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 condensed statements with comparatives are located. Debt note, maturity table and cash-by-entity split are located. Text extraction flattens tables; no original HTML or XBRL is supplied. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description and segments (10-K page:7 to page:14, 10-Q Q3 page:9), the Bausch + Lomb ownership and separation status (10-Q Q3 page:9 to page:10), the refinancing history (10-Q Q3 page:29 to page:30) and subsequent events (10-Q Q3 page:76) are located. Executed debt documents and Bausch + Lomb's own filings are not supplied. |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Can synthesize from CP-1 and CP-1A plus located covenant, liquidity, rating and litigation text. The covenant ratio and the Covenant Step Up Date are not in the pack. |
| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every source has stable chunk numbers, so claims can be traced. Layout and table-fidelity checks against the filed HTML cannot be done from text extraction. |
### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited consolidated statements. page:1 reads "For the Fiscal Year Ended December 31, 2025" and "Commission File Number: 001-14956". Directors' signature dates on page:211 are February 2026, and the liquidity section dates revolver availability "As of February 18, 2026" (page:176).

- Audit: page:211 index lists "Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (PCAOB ID 238)"; page:215 presents critical audit matters (Medicaid rebates and sales returns allowances; goodwill impairment assessments of the Salix and Generics reporting units, page:217).

- Statements and notes located: balance sheet page:218, cash flows page:220, financing note "10.FINANCING ARRANGEMENTS" starting page:269 with the instrument table, maturities at page:56, page:136 and page:173, lease note at page:301, segment note referenced as Note 23.

- Perimeter: consolidated Bausch Health Companies Inc. with noncontrolling interest, including Bausch + Lomb. Currency: USD per the context; the Q3 10-Q states that "references to “$” are to United States (“U.S.”) dollars" (page:3). A statement of currency inside the 10-K itself was not located by search, so the 10-K currency rests on the context setting and the table headings.
#### Forms 10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 (three files)

- Family and authority: filed, unaudited quarterly reports. Each cover page states its period: "For the Quarterly Period Ended March 31, 2026" (Q1 page:1), "June 30, 2026" (Q2 page:1) and "September 30, 2026" (Q3 page:1).

- Q3 10-Q statements: balance sheet at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (page:5 to page:6), statements of operations for three and nine months (page:6), cash flows for nine months (page:8). Note 10 "FINANCING ARRANGEMENTS" at page:27, covenant compliance at page:28 to page:29, 2025 Senior Secured Credit Facilities and covenant terms at page:31 to page:34, Bausch + Lomb facilities at page:34 to page:38, maturities at page:42, Note 17 legal proceedings from page:50, Note 18 segment information at page:74, Note 19 subsequent events at page:76. MD&A liquidity at page:126 to page:133, revolver availability and credit ratings at page:131.

- Q1 10-Q: balance sheet page:5, cash flows page:7, financing note page:25 onward, availability page:116. Q2 10-Q: balance sheet page:5, cash flows page:7, financing note page:26 onward, availability page:127.

- Version relationship: the Q3 report carries December 31, 2025 balance sheet comparatives; the quarterly reports are separate active sources, not replacements for one another. Q1 and Q2 are needed for discrete-quarter and nine-month movement; the Q3 report carries three-month and nine-month columns.
#### Earnings releases (three files, Exhibit 99.1)
- Family and authority: management-prepared, unaudited, furnished with Form 8-K. Datelines: "LAVAL, QC, April 29, 2026", "July 29, 2026", "October 28, 2026".

- Content: reported revenue by segment, adjusted EBITDA reconciliation for Bausch Health, Bausch + Lomb and "Bausch Health (excl. B+L)" (Q3 release page:28), adjusted net income reconciliation (page:22), adjusted cash flow reconciliation (page:27), debt maturity table (page:27) and full-year guidance (page:4).

- These are attributed supporting claims. Adjusted measures are management-defined and not GAAP. Where a release and a 10-Q state the same item, the 10-Q controls. The Q3 release states consolidated "Cash provided by operating activities $ 813" for the three months (page:27), a quarter-only figure; the Q3 10-Q cash flow statement is nine-month (page:8).
### Information-availability boundary

- All seven documents are dated on or before the cutoff. The latest are the Q3 release (October 28, 2026) and the Q3 10-Q, whose cover gives shares outstanding "as of October 23, 2026" (page:1) and whose subsequent-events note refers to October 29, 2026 (page:76).

- Nothing dated after the Q3 10-Q and Q3 release and before 2026-11-05 is supplied. Events in that window are Not supplied, not absent.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Bausch Health Companies Inc., a British Columbia, Canada company; common shares on the NYSE and TSX under BHC (Q3 10-Q page:1). Statements are consolidated with its subsidiaries (page:3).

- Bausch + Lomb: Bausch Health "indirectly holds 310,449,643 common shares of Bausch + Lomb, which represents approximately 87%" (Q3 10-Q page:9). The unaudited statements "do not include any adjustments to give effect to the B+L Separation" (page:10). Consolidated cash is split in the MD&A between Bausch Health and Bausch + Lomb and "is generally not available to support" other entities unless paid as a dividend (page:127).

("BHA") issues certain Senior Unsecured Notes (page:39); Bausch + Lomb is borrower under the B+L credit facilities and issuer of the B+L Senior Secured Notes (page:34 to page:38).

- Restricted and unrestricted status: 126NumberCo is a non-guarantor restricted subsidiary under the Existing Senior Notes indentures (page:30). Bausch + Lomb and its subsidiaries "continue to be unrestricted subsidiaries of the Company" and its earnings and net debt are excluded from the financial maintenance covenant calculation (page:40).

### Debt, liquidity and covenant evidence located (for downstream use; not calculated here)

- Instrument table: Q3 10-Q page:27 lists principal and carrying amounts by instrument at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, with a printed total of "$ 20,168" principal and "20,637" net of premiums, discounts and issuance costs. It includes the 2025 Credit Agreement 2030 Term Loan B Facility, the B+L Credit Facilities, Senior Secured Notes (including the 10.00% Secured Notes due April 2032), the B+L Senior Secured Notes and the Senior Unsecured Notes.
- Maturities: printed for the remainder of 2026 through thereafter (page:42), and split between "Bausch Health debt obligations" and "Bausch + Lomb debt obligations" (page:127 to page:128).

- Revolvers: the 2030 Revolving Credit Facility had "no outstanding borrowings" and "$31 million of issued and outstanding letters of credit" at September 30, 2026 (page:32) and "approximately $469 million of remaining availability" at October 28, 2026 (page:131). The B+L 2030 Revolving Credit Facility had "$100 million of outstanding borrowings" at September 30, 2026 (page:27) and "$666 million of remaining availability" at October 28, 2026 (page:131). Dates differ between the balance sheet and the availability statement.

- Covenants: the 2030 Revolving Credit Facility requires a Blended First Lien Leverage Ratio of not greater than "4.25:1.00" before the Covenant Step Up Date and "5.75:1.00" on and after it, and minimum liquidity of "$400 million" on and after it (page:34). The Company states compliance at September 30, 2026 (page:29). The B+L Term Facilities also contain financial covenants (page:28).
- Ratings as of October 28, 2026 (page:131): Moody's corporate rating Caa2, S&P B-, Fitch B for the Company; Moody's B1 and S&P B for Bausch + Lomb.

- Subsequent events (page:76): Bausch + Lomb CEO transition with a lump-sum payment of approximately "$75 million", a "$50 million" share repurchase authorization dated October 24, 2026, and the announced redemption of "approximately $643 million" of 8.500% Senior Notes due 2027, scheduled for November 30, 2026 and funded with cash on hand.
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: filed statements for FY2025 and Q1 to Q3 2026 allow a consolidated reported view and a split of debt and cash between the parent group and Bausch + Lomb, because the 10-Q prints both splits (page:127 to page:128).

- Strongest contrary evidence: the parent's restricted group excludes Bausch + Lomb for covenant purposes (page:40), while the consolidated statements include it. A consumer reading only consolidated debt would mix two perimeters with different covenants and cash access. The releases present "Bausch Health (excl. B+L)" adjusted EBITDA (Q3 release page:28), which is management's own perimeter and not a covenant definition.

- Source risk mechanism: the covenant ratio is defined by terms of the 2025 Credit Agreement, which is not supplied, and no source prints the reported ratio or the Covenant Step Up Date. Evidence of a threshold without a numerator, a denominator or a date means headroom cannot be sourced and any figure computed by a consumer would be the analyst's estimate, not the covenant calculation.

- Premium accounting: the 2022 Exchange was a troubled debt restructuring, so some notes are carried at a premium and interest expense differs from contractual interest (page:40, page:131). Carrying value therefore differs from principal; consumers must state which they use.
- What cannot proceed: covenant headroom on agreement definitions, guarantor-level analysis, collateral-level recovery analysis, Bausch + Lomb standalone credit analysis.

- Next evidence action: supply the 2025 Credit Agreement and indentures (exhibits are listed in the 10-K at page:199 to page:211 but not included), Bausch + Lomb's own Form 10-Q, any compliance certificate or covenant calculation, and filings dated after October 29, 2026 if any.

The Q3 10-Q shows Bausch + Lomb issued the 8.375% Senior Secured Notes due October 2028, while the floating rate notes due January 2031 were issued by its subsidiaries Bausch + Lomb Netherlands B.V. and Bausch & Lomb Incorporated (page:35).
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Reported debt is high but leverage on a derived earnings basis improved through 2026 as earnings rose and cash built; debt maturities cluster in 2028 to 2031, and Bausch + Lomb sits inside the consolidated numbers. | Medium | No adjusted EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025, no interim cash interest and no covenant calculation, so leverage and cover rest on a derived measure. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Consolidated debt to derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments fell at each measured date, from 6.18x at FY2025 to 5.15x at Q3 2026. | Direction is favourable, but gross leverage is still above five times and rests on an earnings measure built from the statements. | Medium |

| Cash interest cover can only be computed for FY2025, at 1.81x; interim cash interest is not printed. | Cover is modest on a cash basis and the 2026 trend cannot be confirmed from the pack. | Medium |

| At September 30, 2026 cash was 2,485 and undrawn revolver capacity was 1,135, but part belongs to Bausch + Lomb. | Liquidity available to the parent group is lower than the consolidated total. | High |

| Maturities are 3,766 in 2028, 1,667 in 2029, 4,123 in 2030 and 3,896 in 2031; 643 of 2027 notes are to be redeemed in cash. | Redemption removes most of the 2027 maturities; refinancing risk moves to 2028 to 2031. | High |
| The revolver covenant levels are printed but the reported ratio and the step-up date are not. | Covenant headroom cannot be verified from the pack. | High |
### Financial base view

The financial base can be built from filed documents: audited FY2025 statements, unaudited Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 statements, and a complete debt table with maturities. Consolidated revenue was 8,317 for nine months 2026 against 7,470 for nine months 2025. Operating income was 773 against 1,339, because nine months 2026 includes a 1,426 goodwill impairment (Q3 10-Q page:6). Before that charge, the derived EBITDA (net income plus tax plus net interest plus depreciation and amortization) was 3,039 for nine months 2026 against 2,397 for nine months 2025. Q3 2026 derived EBITDA of 1,266 matches the release's reported EBITDA line (Q3 release page:24).

Consolidated principal debt was 20,168 at September 30, 2026 against 20,232 at December 31, 2025, so the balance moved little; leverage improved because the earnings denominator rose and cash rose from 1,309 to 2,485. Of the 20,168, Bausch Health (excl. B+L) carries 15,103 and Bausch + Lomb carries 5,065 (page:127 to page:128), and the covenant group excludes Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt (page:40). A consolidated ratio therefore mixes two credit groups. Parent-group net debt fell from 14,198 at December 31, 2025 to 13,130 at September 30, 2026, and by 521 in Q3 2026 alone, consistent with the release's statement of more than 500 of net debt reduction (Q3 release page:1).

Two limits shape every ratio below. First, the pack has no adjusted EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025 (the 10-K prints none), so an LTM adjusted EBITDA is not calculable; the ratios use the statement-derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments, which is not the covenant definition. Second, the 10-Qs print no total cash interest paid, so interim cash interest cover is Not supplied; only FY2025 interest paid of 1,810 (10-K page:319) allows a cash cover figure.

- Operating leases and total lease liabilities: 10-K page:301 shows total lease liabilities of 262 at December 31, 2025 (accrued and other current 61, other non-current 167, financial leases 11 and 23). The Q3 10-Q prints no lease note; operating lease balances at September 30, 2026 are Not supplied.

- Receivables sales: Bausch + Lomb sold receivables for cash proceeds of 26 in nine months 2026 under a true-sale arrangement, all collected and remitted by September 30, 2026 (page:43). The arrangement is outside debt.

### Covenants and ratings

- Revolver maintenance tests (2030 Revolving Credit Facility, page:34): Blended First Lien Leverage Ratio not greater than 4.25:1.00 before the Covenant Step Up Date and 5.75:1.00 on and after it; minimum liquidity of 400 on and after the Covenant Step Up Date. The step-up date is defined in the 2025 Credit Agreement, which is not supplied, and no source prints the reported ratio; the company states compliance at September 30, 2026 (page:29). Headroom is Not calculable.

- The revolver matures at the earlier of April 8, 2030 and 91 days before the scheduled maturity of indebtedness above 1,000 in aggregate principal of the Company or 126NumberCo (page:32). Bausch Health (excl. B+L) has 2,326 of principal due in 2028 (page:127), so this earlier-maturity trigger may apply before April 2030; how the aggregate is measured needs the agreement, which is not supplied.

- No facility of the parent group matures within twelve months of September 30, 2026: the 2030 Revolving Credit Facility matures April 2030 and the B+L 2030 Revolving Credit Facility June 2030 (page:27).

- Ratings at October 28, 2026 (page:131): Moody's Caa2 corporate, Caa1 senior secured, Ca senior unsecured, outlook stable; S&P B- corporate, B- senior secured, CCC+ senior unsecured, outlook negative; Fitch B corporate, BB senior secured, Rating Watch Evolving. Bausch + Lomb: Moody's B1 stable, S&P B with developing outlook. No change to either corporate rating in Q3 2026 (page:132).
### Segment revenue, Q3 2026

Management release, reported basis (Q3 release page:2): Salix 831 against 716; International 299 against 286; Solta Medical 165 against 140; Diversified 271 against 258; Bausch + Lomb 1,375 against 1,281. Bausch Health (excl. B+L) is 1,566 against 1,400. The five segments sum to the consolidated 2,941 against 2,681.
### Interpretation
- Evidence: LTM derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose from 3,276 (FY2025) to 3,918 (LTM Q3 2026) while principal debt moved from 20,232 to 20,168 and cash from 1,309 to 2,485.

- Mechanism: the improvement is earnings and cash driven. Gross debt is flat, so gross leverage of 5.15x at Q3 2026 depends on earnings continuing at the higher level; the company's own guidance for full year adjusted EBITDA of 4,315 to 4,415 (Q3 release page:4) is a management forecast, not a reported figure.

- Perimeter: Bausch + Lomb contributes 328 of the Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of 1,350 and 5,065 of the 20,168 debt (Q3 release page:28; page:127). Its cash and revolver availability are generally not available to the parent group (page:127, page:131). Parent-group net debt is 13,130 against consolidated net debt of 17,683.

- Interest burden: net interest expense of 1,162 for nine months 2026 is a P&L figure reduced by premium amortization; contractual interest is higher. Interest paid in FY2025 was 1,810 against net interest expense of 1,556. The company expects about 561 of interest payments in Q4 2026 (page:133) and the Remaining Secured Notes alone carry 4,017 of scheduled interest payments from the remainder of 2026 to 2032 (page:130).

- Credit implication: leverage is falling but remains high for a group rated Caa2 and B- at the corporate level. Cover on cash interest in FY2025 was 1.81x. The risk is concentrated in 2028 to 2031 maturities and in the structural separation between the parent group and Bausch + Lomb.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| A Xifaxan-dependent U.S. pharmaceutical business sits in one group with Bausch + Lomb through a collateralised holding structure; Salix growth is price-led and Xifaxan faces a Medicare price in 2027 and expected generics in 2028. | Medium | Indentures, the credit agreement and Bausch + Lomb's own filings are not supplied, so legal capacity and creditor rights are described only from filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Salix is about 27% of nine-month 2026 revenue but about 47% of segment profit, and Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix. | Cash generation depends on one product line facing a 2027 Medicare price and 2028 expected generic entry. | High |

| Salix revenue growth of 343 came from price of 504, partly offset by lower volumes of 173 after exiting certain channels. | Growth is price-led; sustainability depends on pricing power that the 2027 negotiated price will limit. | High |

| 211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares are pledged to the 2025 facilities and 2032 notes at 126NumberCo, which ranks ahead of other creditors' claims on those shares. | Creditors outside that structure rank behind it for Bausch + Lomb value. | High |

| The Bausch Health chief executive is also interim chief executive and chairman of Bausch + Lomb, and a 50 buyback was authorised. | Overlapping roles and distributions bear on governance and creditor control, but the amounts are small. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The business is a specialty pharmaceutical and medical device group that sells about 60% of its revenue in the U.S. (FY2025, 10-K page:29) and holds about 87% of Bausch + Lomb, an eye health company that generates nearly half of consolidated revenue (4,013 of 8,317 for nine months 2026, Q3 10-Q page:75). Profit is concentrated: Salix, which sells mainly Xifaxan, produced 1,789 of 3,779 segment profit in nine months 2026 on 2,228 of revenue. The company states that generic Xifaxan is expected in 2028 and that a negotiated Medicare price takes effect on January 1, 2027 (page:96, page:98), and that Salix reporting unit goodwill was impaired by 1,426 after two Phase 3 trials of a new formulation failed in January 2026 (page:26).

The transaction history that matters to creditors is structural. Since 2022 the company has moved Bausch + Lomb shares into a holding company, 126NumberCo, and in 2025 used those shares as collateral for new first-lien debt that extended maturities from 2025 through 2028 to 2030 through 2032 (page:82, page:83). The Existing Senior Secured Notes are structurally subordinated to liabilities of 126NumberCo and to debt secured by assets outside their collateral such as the Bausch + Lomb share collateral (page:39), and the Senior Unsecured Notes are not guaranteed by 126NumberCo or 153NumberCo (page:130). Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are excluded from the parent's financial maintenance covenant (page:40). Creditors therefore hold a claim on a group whose most valuable subsidiary sits in a separate credit silo, and the company has described a full separation of Bausch + Lomb as subject to targeted leverage ratios and approvals (page:10). Net proceeds from any sale of the pledged shares must be applied to prepay the 2025 term loan and the 2032 notes pro rata (page:33, page:38).

Recent operating momentum is real but price-led, and the legal and regulatory calendar is dense. The main uncertainties for monitoring are the Xifaxan price and generic timeline, the Bausch + Lomb separation path, refinancing of the 2028 to 2031 maturities, and the unsupplied debt documents.

| Management view of the portfolio | "The Company remains committed to evaluating all options for unlocking shareholder value, including maximizing the value of our Bausch Health and Bausch + Lomb assets." | Management Language | Q3 release page:4 |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition or leveraged buyout is pending at the issuer; the transactions that matter are financing and structural, and all are described from filings, not from the executed documents, which are not supplied.

The 2022 Exchange closed on September 30, 2022: validly tendered senior unsecured notes of 5,594 were exchanged for 3,125 of new secured notes, a reduction of principal of 2,469, and the company concluded it met the criteria for a troubled debt restructuring under ASC 470-60 (Q3 10-Q page:40). On November 29, 2022 the company designated 126NumberCo, which holds Bausch + Lomb, as an unrestricted subsidiary, so Bausch + Lomb and its subsidiaries are outside the covenants of the Bausch Health debt documents (page:39, page:40). In March 2025, in connection with the April 2025 refinancing, 126NumberCo was re-designated a restricted subsidiary while Bausch + Lomb and its subsidiaries remained unrestricted (page:40).

The April 2025 Refinancing Transactions closed on April 8, 2025: 126NumberCo entered the 2025 Credit Agreement (a 500 five-year revolving credit facility due April 8, 2030 and a 3,000 term loan B due October 8, 2030) and issued 4,400 of 10.00% senior secured notes due April 15, 2032. Proceeds repaid or redeemed 6,870 of principal in total (the February 2027 term loan B of 2,156 and certain notes), which the company says extended approximately 6,870 of maturities from 2025 through 2028 to 2030 through 2032 (page:29, page:82, page:83). In August 2025 the company repurchased and retired 9.25% senior unsecured notes of about 602 par for about 601 of cash on hand (page:40). In December 2025 the company and 126NumberCo exchanged 797 of 4.875% senior secured notes due 2028 and 886 of 11.00% first lien notes due 2028 for 1,600 of new 10.00% senior secured notes due April 2032, which form one series with the earlier 2032 notes, reducing outstanding principal by 83; 26,495,472 Bausch + Lomb shares were transferred to 126NumberCo as part of the transaction and the exchange was accounted for as a modification, not a troubled debt restructuring (page:30, page:83, page:84).

At Bausch + Lomb, the June 2025 refinancing added an 800 revolving credit facility due June 26, 2030, a 2,325 term loan B due January 15, 2031 and EUR 675 floating rate notes due January 2031; in January 2026 a new 2,802 term loan facility due January 15, 2031 refinanced the 2028 and 2031 term loans in full (page:35, page:36, page:84). No new bond issue by the parent is described for 2026 in the pages read; nine months 2026 issuance of long-term debt of 2,930 is described as primarily the 2,802 of Bausch + Lomb refinancing proceeds and 75 of revolver borrowings (page:126).

After the quarter, the company announced on October 28, 2026 that its subsidiary Bausch Health Americas, Inc. will issue an irrevocable redemption notice on October 29, 2026 for all of its 8.500% senior notes due 2027, about 643 of principal, with redemption scheduled for November 30, 2026 and funded from cash on hand (page:76). This is a subsequent event and is not in any September 30, 2026 balance. The board also authorised a share repurchase of up to 50 on October 24, 2026, aimed at offsetting dilution from 2027 management equity vesting per the release (page:76; Q3 release page:1). Bausch + Lomb agreed on October 8, 2026 to buy ophthalmic surgical manufacturing businesses for about 85 upfront, due at closing in the fourth quarter of 2026 (page:18).

Other transactions affecting business risk: the December 2025 acquisition of the aesthetics distribution business of Solta's China distributor for about 87 aggregate consideration (page:15); the September 2025 DURECT acquisition for 84 with potential sales-based milestones of up to 350 (page:17); and a December 2025 Bausch + Lomb purchase of manufacturing equipment for about 75 upfront with up to 35 of milestones (page:17).
### Ownership, control and creditor structure
| Item | Fact | Category | Locator |

| Collateral for 2025 facilities and 2032 notes | First priority lien on substantially all assets of 126NumberCo, including 211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares (the Bausch + Lomb Share Collateral); guaranteed by the Company and subsidiaries with secured guarantees | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:31, page:37 |

| Legal capacity (indentures, credit agreement) | Debt capacity, restricted payment, asset sale and designation baskets are not in the pack | Insufficient Information | CP-0 handoff; 10-K page:199 to page:211 (exhibit list only) |
### Governance and sponsor behavior

Assessed at issuer level from documented actions. The legal capacity column states what the documents are known to permit, willingness what was done, feasibility the liquidity and market access shown in CP-1.

### Timeline

### Legal and regulatory items with credit relevance

- Xifaxan: settled Paragraph IV cases are noted; Norwich's first ANDA is enjoined from final FDA approval until October 2029 (page:57); a second Norwich ANDA is in litigation, with a summary judgment hearing on October 7, 2026 and no trial date set (page:58); a DC Circuit opinion of August 25, 2026 partly reversed a lower court on Norwich's forfeiture theory and remanded to the FDA, and Teva's rehearing petition was denied on October 28, 2026 (page:58). The company still lists Xifaxan loss of exclusivity as expected in 2028 (page:98). The effect on the 2028 date is not quantified in the pack.
- Antitrust class actions allege the 2018 Actavis Xifaxan settlement is anticompetitive (page:55); no amount is quantified.

- Talc: remaining Shower to Shower suits are "subject to full indemnification obligations of Johnson & Johnson" (page:62), and the company expects not to incur material losses (page:64). This rests on the indemnitor's performance, which the pack does not test.

- Tax: Luxembourg assessment of EUR 271.7 million excluding interest; unfavourable ruling in March 2026, appeal heard October 15, 2026; no reserve recorded (page:48). The judgment, expected within 90 days of the hearing, is not in the pack.
- Pricing policy: the IRA negotiated price for Xifaxan applies from 2027; the company says the impact is expected to be most significant during 2027 (page:96).

| Conflict | Source A (quote) | Source B (quote) | Downstream effect |

| Interest payments charged against debt premium, nine months 2026 | Q3 10-Q page:126: "$158 million of contractual interest payments on the Remaining Secured Notes (as defined below) allocated to the reduction of the recorded premiums" | Q3 release page:27: "Interest payments charged against debt premium (44) (87) (144) (251)" | Not reconciled here. The filing governs the premium accounting; the release's adjusted cash flow from operations uses its own figure. Same item as logged in CP-1. |

No other disagreement between sources was found for items used in this module. Where the company says Xifaxan generics are expected in 2028 and Norwich's first ANDA is enjoined until October 2029, these concern different applicants and are not a conflict on the same fact.
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability and concentration. Evidence: Salix is about 27% of revenue and about 47% of segment profit, Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix, growth was price-led (price 504, volumes down 173), a negotiated price starts January 1, 2027 and generic entry is expected in 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:75, page:123, page:96, page:98). Risk mechanic: the product that earns the largest share of segment profit faces a price reset and then volume erosion just as 2028 maturities of 3,766 become due (CP-1). Credit implication: refinancing capacity in 2028 depends on how much Xifaxan cash flow remains, which makes monitoring of Xifaxan sales, the 2027 price effect and the generic timeline a leading indicator for refinancing risk. Counter-evidence: Salix profit rose 28% in nine months 2026 and management raised guidance; neither tests the post-2027 level.

2. Structural subordination and the Bausch + Lomb silo. Evidence: first-lien claims at 126NumberCo hold the pledged Bausch + Lomb shares, and other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind (page:31, page:39); Bausch + Lomb's net debt and earnings are outside the covenant perimeter (page:40). Risk mechanic: value from the Bausch + Lomb stake flows first to the 2025 term loan and 2032 notes through the sweep (page:33, page:38). Credit implication: recovery prospects for notes outside that structure depend on residual value in the shares and on Bausch Health (excl. B+L) assets, with no expected recovery stated here.

3. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose to 3,918 on an LTM basis, while FY2025 cash interest cover was 1.81x on interest paid of 1,810 (CP-1). Risk mechanic: high cash interest and premium accounting mean P&L interest understates cash cost. Credit implication: cover is modest on a cash basis, so a decline in Salix profit would reduce cover quickly.

4. Sponsor and governance alignment. Evidence: no dividends and a small buyback, an issuer-level pattern of maturity extension, but unresolved participation terms in exchanges and overlapping leadership of two listed entities (page:127, page:76, page:138). Credit implication: mixed; the pack neither shows leakage nor tests the indentures' restrictions.
5. Key uncertainties. The covenant ratio and its step-up date, the debt document baskets, and the 2028 maturity wall (CP-0, CP-1).
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Readiness | What it should take from this module | Why it matters | Gap | Required action |

| CP-2 | Ready with limitations | Product concentration, price-led growth, 2027 and 2028 Xifaxan timeline, structural subordination, governance observations, timeline of events | These drive the credit assessment and the thesis | Debt documents and Bausch + Lomb filings not supplied; fourth quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA not supplied | Carry gaps into CP-2 gaps ledger; do not state a recovery outcome |

| CP-5 | Ready with limitations | All locators here are chunk numbers with quoted spans; derived percentages are labelled Analyst Interpretation | Evidence trace validation | Text extraction only | Check the derived shares (27%, 47%, 23%, 68%) against the cited figures |
## Calculations
Inputs are printed figures from the cited pages. All amounts US$ millions unless stated.
- Salix share of revenue, nine months 2026: 2,228 / 8,317 = 26.8%, stated as about 27%.
- Salix share of segment profit, nine months 2026: 1,789 / 3,779 = 47.3%, stated as about 47%.
- Xifaxan revenue, approximate: 0.85 × 2,228 = 1,894; 1,894 / 8,317 = 22.8%, stated as about 23%. The 85% is printed as "approximately".
- Bausch + Lomb share of revenue: 4,013 / 8,317 = 48.3%; of segment profit: 1,022 / 3,779 = 27.0%.
- Salix revenue change: 2,228 − 1,885 = 343, equal to price 504 plus discontinued products 12 less volumes 173 (504 + 12 − 173 = 343). Percent change 343 / 1,885 = 18.2%, printed as 18%.
- Pledged Bausch + Lomb shares: 211,963,893 / 310,449,643 = 68.3%; unpledged or elsewhere: 310,449,643 − 211,963,893 = 98,485,750 shares (holder not stated).
- Wholesaler concentration FY2025: 18% + 16% + 14% = 48%.
- Dec 2025 exchange: 797 + 886 = 1,683 exchanged for 1,600 new, a reduction of 83, as printed.
- Redemption of 643 of 2027 notes: see CP-1 for the pro forma maturity effect (701 − 643 = 58 consolidated).
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Indentures, 2025 Credit Agreement, intercreditor and collateral documents not supplied: legal capacity for designations, exchanges, restricted payments and debt incurrence cannot be assessed | High | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply executed documents from the 10-K exhibit list (10-K page:199 to page:211) |
| Participation terms of the 2022 and December 2025 exchanges (pro rata or selective) not in the pack | High | CP-2 | Supply exchange offer documents and 8-Ks |
| Holder and pledge status of the 98,485,750 Bausch + Lomb shares outside the 126NumberCo holding | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the 2025 Credit Agreement collateral schedule or Bausch + Lomb disclosures |
| Beneficial ownership table and any controlling or significant shareholder | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the proxy statement |
| Bausch + Lomb standalone filings, covenants and governance | Medium | CP-2 | Supply Bausch + Lomb Form 10-Q and credit agreement |
| Quantified effect of the 2027 negotiated Xifaxan price and of generic entry on revenue and profit | High | CP-2 | Not disclosed in the pack; request management detail or monitor quarterly |
| Covenant certificate and covenant-definition add-back bridge not supplied | High | CP-2 | Supply compliance certificate and 2025 Credit Agreement definitions |
| Outcomes of legal and tax matters after October 29, 2026, including the Luxembourg appeal judgment and November 3, 2026 mediation | Medium | CP-2 | Supply later filings |
| Text extraction only; no check against filed HTML | Low | CP-5 | Supply original HTML or XBRL |
## Next module

CP-2 follows with the fundamental credit synthesis, taking from this module: the concentration of profit in Salix and Xifaxan, the price-led growth, the January 1, 2027 negotiated price and expected 2028 generic entry, the Bausch + Lomb collateral and covenant perimeter structure, the mixed governance observations and the unresolved legal capacity, and the logged conflict on interest charged against premium. CP-2 should keep CP-1's figures (LTM derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments 3,918; debt to EBITDA 5.15x; net 4.51x) and carry every gap above. CP-5 then traces the evidence.

spans.text: # CP-2 — Fundamental credit synthesis: Bausch Health Companies Inc. (bhc)
## Request

This module synthesises the fundamental credit view of Bausch Health Companies Inc. (issuer id `bhc`) as of 2026-11-05, for the credit_snapshot pathway, from the CP-1 financial base and the CP-1A business and transaction context. It uses upstream handoffs only and adds no new source reading; it gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. Amounts are USD millions as reported by the issuer, and periods are labelled Q3 2026, nine months 2026, FY2025 and LTM Q3 2026.
## Sources
Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs (page-numbered text extractions pinned by CP-OS; this module read none of them directly and relies on the handoffs below for every figure):
| Source | sha256 | Role |
| 10-Q_2026-03-31_bhc-20260331.htm.jsonl | 2ab4f9a58a29bd8e4f27c1aaa3b34a916ad63a6c5e24a2f2cf1f677d2bf1adb3 | Form 10-Q for Q1 2026 |

| EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991-q22026.htm.jsonl | b572ec3ee8791446c7753f44c437564f85dc7c22a9282dc8fe3094943c7ca9ed | Q2 2026 earnings release (management) |
| EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl | d176e2b2337e8c9ee765792690a4c9894f8e78c9eadadca91a11afce842a8bb9 | Q3 2026 earnings release (management) |
| context | ce3ba040ad702f7a097a4705cf09e05a5541c48113a20eaf4b83ee334242bc43 | User run settings; not issuer evidence |
Supplied handoffs:
| Module | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | f3a9713066d902ea831e33ca5e21c7518220ff0fc6d8658f54808a4e8892a5bd | Source readiness and gaps |
| CP-1 | 6416762ec0c950756779b461584b370e27dfe8cc5ec45b3b126353256df99610 | Financial base, leverage, liquidity, maturities, premium accounting conflict |
| CP-1A | 44d95c2186bb66af7e9424745c7b2701139cffc88c48dc61707f41e82211ccb3 | Business, ownership, transaction, governance, legal items |

Consistency with the handoffs: the CP-1 correction to CP-0 on the Bausch + Lomb note issuers stands. This module repeats CP-1 and CP-1A figures without change and recomputes only the sums shown in `## Calculations`.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Bausch Health is a highly leveraged credit on an improving path: leverage and liquidity improved in 2026, but profit depends on Xifaxan ahead of a 2027 price reset and the 2028 to 2031 maturities remain large. | Medium | No debt documents, covenant calculation or fourth quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA are supplied, so headroom, legal capacity and an adjusted leverage ratio cannot be verified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Consolidated debt to derived EBITDA fell from 6.18x at FY2025 to 5.15x at Q3 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 4.51x. | The direction is favourable, but leverage remains high for a group rated Caa2 and B- at the corporate level. | Medium |

| Salix produced about 47% of segment profit, and Xifaxan faces a negotiated price from January 1, 2027 and expected generics in 2028. | Refinancing capacity in 2028 depends on Xifaxan cash flow surviving the price reset. | High |
| Maturities total 13,452 across 2028 to 2031, and 643 of 2027 notes are to be redeemed from cash. | Cash used for the redemption reduces the buffer ahead of the 2028 maturities. | Medium |
| Bausch + Lomb shares are pledged to the 2025 first-lien debt, and Bausch + Lomb sits outside the covenant group. | Creditors outside that structure rank behind it for Bausch + Lomb value. | High |
| Cash interest cover was 1.81x in FY2025, and interim cash interest cover is not supplied. | Debt service capacity is modest and the 2026 improvement cannot be confirmed on a cash basis. | Medium |
### Credit view

Bausch Health is a highly leveraged, structurally complex credit that is improving but not yet resilient. Its strongest support is liquidity and momentum: USD 2,485 million of consolidated cash and USD 1,135 million of undrawn revolvers at September 30, 2026, derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million, and debt to that EBITDA down from 6.18x to 5.15x [CP-1]. Its weakest point is dependence on Salix and Xifaxan, about 47% of segment profit, which faces a negotiated Medicare price from 2027 and expected generics in 2028, just before USD 3,766 million of debt falls due in 2028 [CP-1A, CP-1]. The outcome turns on how much Xifaxan cash flow survives 2027, and on whether USD 13,452 million due in 2028 to 2031 is refinanced inside a structure that ranks Bausch + Lomb value to the 2025 first-lien debt first.
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Highly leveraged and structurally complex, with improving earnings, cash and maturity profile, and concentrated product risk in 2027 and 2028 | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and maturities; CP-1A concentration, structure and timeline |

| Thesis | Bausch Health's debt service and refinancing capacity rest on Salix and Xifaxan cash flow holding through the 2027 price reset, while Bausch + Lomb value is committed first to the 2025 first-lien debt | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A operating model, ownership and creditor structure; CP-1 maturities |

| Confidence limits | Medium, not High: the debt documents, the covenant ratio and its step-up date, the fourth quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA and the participation terms of past exchanges are not supplied | Insufficient Information | Medium | CP-0 and CP-1 gaps; CP-1A gaps |
### Key findings

1. Leverage is falling but high. Consolidated principal debt of USD 20,168 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 20,232 million at December 31, 2025) over derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million gives 5.15x gross and 4.51x net, against 6.18x and 5.78x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Debt barely moved, so the improvement comes from earnings and from cash rising to USD 2,485 million. [Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is a derived Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure.]

2. The parent group deleveraged in Q3 2026. Bausch Health (excl. B+L) net debt fell from USD 13,651 million to USD 13,130 million, a reduction of USD 521 million in the quarter, while its debt was USD 15,103 million [CP-1]. Bausch + Lomb debt was USD 5,065 million and its cash and revolver are generally not available to the parent [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the net debt figures are derived.]

3. Liquidity is adequate near term but thinner at the parent. Consolidated cash plus undrawn revolvers was USD 3,620 million; the parent's share was USD 2,442 million (cash USD 1,973 million including restricted cash, plus USD 469 million undrawn) [CP-1]. The USD 643 million 2027 notes will be redeemed from cash on November 30, 2026, which reduces parent liquidity to about USD 1,799 million pro forma [CP-1, calculation below]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

4. The maturity wall starts in 2028. Debt maturing is USD 15 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 701 million in 2027, USD 3,766 million in 2028, USD 1,667 million in 2029, USD 4,123 million in 2030 and USD 3,896 million in 2031, with USD 6,000 million thereafter [CP-1]. The parent's 2028 maturities of USD 2,326 million exceed its pro forma liquidity of about USD 1,799 million, so repayment relies on cash generation or refinancing; the revolver also has an earlier-maturity trigger tied to indebtedness above USD 1,000 million [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

5. Earnings quality is price-led and concentrated. Salix revenue rose USD 343 million in nine months 2026 on price of USD 504 million, partly offset by volumes down USD 173 million, and Salix is about 27% of revenue but about 47% of segment profit [CP-1A]. Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix, faces a negotiated Medicare price from January 1, 2027 and expected generics in 2028, and the company impaired Salix goodwill by USD 1,426 million in January 2026 after failed Phase 3 trials [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the concentration shares are derived.]

6. Cash interest absorbs a large share of earnings. FY2025 cash interest was USD 1,810 million against derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,276 million, about 55% of it and a cover of 1.81x, and the pack gives no interim cash interest [CP-1]. Premium accounting makes P&L interest lower than cash interest, so cover on a P&L basis (2.53x LTM Q3 2026) is flattered [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact for inputs; Analyst Interpretation on direction.]

7. Structure matters as much as leverage. The 2025 first-lien debt at 126NumberCo holds a lien on 211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares, and sales proceeds must prepay it pro rata with the 2032 notes; other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind, and Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are outside the covenant [CP-1A]. Legal capacity and exchange terms cannot be tested without the debt documents. [Documentary Fact.]

8. Governance evidence is mixed rather than adverse. No dividends and a USD 50 million buyback authorised, a cash repurchase of near-par unsecured notes in 2025 and extended maturities weigh against overlapping leadership of two listed entities and unresolved terms of exchanges [CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.]
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths:

- Earnings recovery with deleveraging. Derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose from USD 3,276 million (FY2025) to USD 3,918 million (LTM Q3 2026) while principal debt stayed near USD 20,200 million, lowering gross leverage by about one turn [CP-1]. This reduces default risk on a going-concern basis. [Analyst Interpretation.]

- Refinancing already done. The 2025 refinancing and the December 2025 exchange extended about USD 6,870 million and USD 1,600 million of maturities to 2030 through 2032, so only USD 716 million falls due before 2028 on a consolidated basis, and USD 643 million of that is to be redeemed from cash [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact for the transactions; the 716 sum is derived.]
- Cash and parent deleveraging. Cash of USD 2,485 million and parent net debt down USD 521 million in Q3 2026 show cash generation reaching the parent group [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact.]

- Covenant exposure is limited and stated compliant. The revolver has two maintenance tests, and the company states compliance at September 30, 2026 [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact; the headroom is Not supplied.]

- Diversification outside Salix. International, Solta Medical and Bausch + Lomb grew in nine months 2026, and Bausch + Lomb produced about 27% of segment profit [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the share is derived.]
- No shareholder leakage. No dividends in FY2025, FY2024 or FY2023, and restrictions in the debt documents [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.]
Weaknesses:

- Product concentration with dated erosion. Salix and Xifaxan dominate segment profit, and the negotiated price and generic entry are dated [CP-1A]. Mechanic: price-led growth meets a price cap, then volume loss. Implication: lower cash available for 2028 refinancing. [Documentary Fact for the dates; Analyst Interpretation on the effect.]
- High leverage and modest cash cover. 5.15x gross leverage and 1.81x FY2025 cash interest cover leave limited tolerance for a profit decline [CP-1]. [Analyst Interpretation.]
- Large 2028 to 2031 maturities, USD 13,452 million in total, with USD 8,422 million of it at the parent [CP-1, calculation below]. [Analyst Interpretation.]
- Structural subordination and a separate Bausch + Lomb silo. Value in the Bausch + Lomb stake serves the 2025 first-lien debt first, and its cash is generally trapped [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.]
- Weak credit ratings: Moody's Caa2 and S&P B- corporate, with a negative outlook at S&P and Rating Watch Evolving at Fitch [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.]

- Litigation and regulatory exposure: antitrust class actions on the Xifaxan settlement, a Luxembourg tax assessment with no reserve, an FDA warning letter at a Bausch + Lomb plant, and talc claims backed by an indemnity from Johnson & Johnson whose performance the pack does not test [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; amounts of exposure are Not supplied.]

- Opaque adjusted measures. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted cash flow are management-defined, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is missing, so no adjusted LTM leverage exists [CP-0, CP-1]. [Insufficient Information.]
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category |

| Xifaxan price reset and generic entry | Negotiated Medicare price from 2027 and expected generics in 2028 hit a product that supplies most of Salix profit, after price-led growth | Lower cash available for 2028 maturities; leverage tolerance falls | Critical | Documentary Fact for dates; Analyst Interpretation for effect |

| Refinancing of 2028 to 2031 maturities | USD 13,452 million falls due across four years while the revolver may mature earlier under its trigger, and cash is used for the 2027 notes redemption | Reliance on market access at a Caa2 and B- corporate rating; cost of debt may rise | Critical | Analyst Interpretation |

| Leverage and interest burden | 5.15x gross leverage, 1.81x FY2025 cash interest cover, premium accounting masks cash interest | Little tolerance for earnings decline; debt service sensitive to rates on variable debt | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Structural subordination and Bausch + Lomb silo | First-lien claims at 126NumberCo have priority on the pledged shares; Bausch + Lomb cash and earnings are outside the parent covenant | Recovery prospects for creditors outside the structure depend on residual value; no recovery outcome is stated | Material | Documentary Fact |

| Unsupplied covenant and document terms | Covenant ratio, step-up date, baskets and exchange terms are not in the pack | Headroom and creditor protection cannot be verified | Material | Insufficient Information |
| Legal and regulatory | Antitrust, tax, talc indemnity reliance, FDA findings | Cash payments or earnings loss if outcomes adverse; amounts not supplied | Material | Documentary Fact |

| Governance and separation path | Overlapping leadership; separation subject to leverage targets and approvals | Uncertain timing and form of any separation affects collateral value and creditor control | Minor | Analyst Interpretation |
## Calculations
Inputs are the figures stated in the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs. All amounts USD millions.
- Maturities before 2028, consolidated: 15 + 701 = 716; after the 643 redemption: 716 − 643 = 73.

- Parent liquidity, September 30, 2026: cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash 1,973 + undrawn 2030 Revolving Credit Facility 469 = 2,442. Pro forma for the redemption of 643 funded from cash: 2,442 − 643 = 1,799. The pro forma ignores any redemption premium, accrued interest, fourth quarter interest of about 561 consolidated, capital expenditure and cash generation after September 30, 2026.
- Pro forma parent liquidity against 2028 parent maturities: 1,799 / 2,326 = 0.77x.

- Parent cash generation, nine months 2026, management's adjusted cash flows from operations for Bausch Health (excl. B+L): 319 (Q1) + 471 (Q2) + 539 (Q3) = 1,329.
